Asset: WELL-0149 (NE-07 Well 149, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 21 May 2023 08:00 · Finished: 23 May 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 63 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0149-0030 on 2023-05-18 Report written: 24 May 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0149-0030 showed the wellhead at 36.3 °C with the air at 25.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0149-005 (WS-06).

Asset: WELL-0149 (NE-07 Well 149, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 04 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 21 Aug 2023 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 422 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0149-0041 on 2023-08-03 Report written: 21 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0149-0041 showed the wellhead at 36.2 °C with the air at 32.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 381 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 305 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0149-006 (WS-06).

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0149-020

Asset: WELL-0149 (NE-07 Well 149, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 01 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 02 Aug 2025 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 27 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0149-0145 on 2025-07-31 Report written: 02 Aug 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0149-0145 at 07:45 on 2025-07-31 found crude oil on the pad: about 10.1% of the pad area, estimated 4.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 381 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 305 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0149-020 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.57% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
